caption: The drawing depicts two views of a metallic lantern mounted on a pole. The lantern features a tall, narrow, and hexagonal body with a pointed, vented roof, which is adorned with circular dot patterns. At the front, the lantern has a rectangular glass door or window, through which a candle placed inside is visible. The lower section of the lantern extends outward in a conical shape, decorated centrally with a radiating rosette pattern of stamped or embossed metalwork. The pole supporting the lantern is cylindrical and features a spiral groove running along its length, giving it a twisted appearance. The entire drawing uses gray and black pencil or ink lines for outlines and hatching, with shading to suggest metallic texture and three-dimensionality. The background is left plain and uncolored, with the focus solely on the lantern and its structural details. In the bottom right corner, there is text that reads "Master C. Closson - Taos - N.M."
title: Penitente Processional Lantern
cluster: #16 — Lighting Devices: Lamps, Lanterns, and Candleholders
